- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior peak unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (avg between -0.3 and +0.3), model underestimates volatility — increase forecast variance by 10–15% in early horizon (1–3 days) to reflect uncertainty.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend + negative sentiment, model often fails to reverse — add 2–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days to capture reversion.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate short-term volatility — reduce forecast slope by 15–20% in first 7–10 days if sentiment is weak or neutral.
- When sentiment is strongly bullish (avg > +0.7) and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate sudden pullback — add 1–2% downward buffer in 10–15 day horizon if recent price is >15% above 10-day avg.
